- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3-day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average of history, adjust forecast toward historical mean (not latest peak or trough).
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit recent noise; use 7-day weighted average of history for smoothing.
